claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if future filings drop the substrate-chain and sole-source language (dependency resolved via second sources), or if InP substrate supply normalizes (pricing/lead-time reversion disclosed by suppliers); upgrade when Lumentum names substrate suppliers or quantifies advance payments to them, or a supplier names Lumentum as committed customer.
claims.statement: Lumentum's audited FY2026 10-K provides the first statutory customer-side document for its substrate dependency: some suppliers are sole sources for certain materials; Lumentum has made advance payments to secure orders (customer-to-supplier costly commitment) while honestly disclosing it lacks long-term agreements with many suppliers; and China's export restrictions to Japan 'affected our substrate supply chain globally'. This upgrades the LITE→InP-substrate edge from transcript/news evidence to statutory filing grade. Honest limit: the 10-K never names indium phosphide substrates specifically — InP-specificity still rests on existing earnings-call and Reuters assertions; advance-payment counterparties and amounts are undisclosed.

source_doc.title: Lumentum Holdings FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-08-17)

sources.quote: We purchase raw materials, packages and components from a limited number of suppliers, who are often small and specialized. Additionally, some of our suppliers are our sole sources for certain materials, equipment and components.
While we have entered into advanced payments to secure orders from some of these suppliers, we have not entered into long-term agreements with many of these suppliers.
Similarly, China restricted exports to Japan, which affected our substrate supply chain globally.

sources.locator: Item 1 — Sources and Availability of Raw Materials
sources.quote: Although our intention is to establish at least two sources of supply for materials whenever possible, for certain components we have sole or limited source supply arrangements.
